rows.selection_reason: With no prior evidence, the first experiment should establish a strong multimodal baseline to anchor all subsequent comparisons. config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) combines the most promising design choices: multiprofile for richer cell-level information, scgpt as a well-established pretrained RNA encoder, resnet50 as a solid yet relatively fast image backbone, avgpool for efficient multiprofile aggregation, and weighted fusion as a standard multimodal combination strategy. This tests the core hypothesis that combining RNA and image modalities with a strong encoder pair yields high validation accuracy. It is cost-moderate (resnet50 + avgpool is cheaper than imagenet_vit_l + transformer, but more expensive than single-modality baselines), making it an efficient first probe. The resulting accuracy will serve as the reference point for later ablations (e.g., swapping to imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, scvi_n200, or singleprofile) in the remaining 9 experiments.

With only one completed experiment (config_002, multimodal/multiprofile/scgpt/resnet50/avgpool/weighted at 52.5% acc, 4.42 GPU hrs), the most critical uncertainty is whether the multimodal combination is actually contributing over a single modality, or whether one modality dominates. config_005 (image_only, singleprofile, resnet50) is the cheapest possible informative experiment—no RNA encoder, single profile (no aggregation), and resnet50 is a standard pretrained encoder—so expected cost is roughly 0.5–1.0 GPU hours, far below config_002. If image-only accuracy is close to 52.5%, RNA adds little value under this setup and future experiments should focus on image-encoder upgrades (e.g., ViT-L) or fusion refinements. If image-only is substantially lower (e.g., <40%), the RNA modality is clearly contributing and we should exploit that by testing RNA-encoder variants (scvi_n200, pca_n2000) and aggregation strategies. This single cheap experiment partitions the 8 remaining budget much more effectively than a second multimodal run, which would only give a small incremental signal on one sub-dimension while leaving the modality-contribution question unresolved.

Evidence: config_002 (scgpt, resnet50, avgpool, weighted, multiprofile) achieves 0.525 acc, while image-only (config_005) is only 0.208, confirming both modalities contribute. The single most impactful untested dimension is the image backbone: upgrading resnet50 (~25M params) to imagenet_vit_l (~300M params) is the largest representational capacity jump available. This experiment (config_018) changes only the image encoder from resnet50 to imagenet_vit_l while holding all other settings identical to the current best (scgpt, multiprofile, avgpool, weighted), isolating the effect of a stronger visual backbone. If it improves accuracy meaningfully, subsequent experiments can exploit ViT-L with transformer aggregation or different fusion; if it does not, we redirect to RNA-encoder or aggregation changes. Expected relative cost: roughly 2–3× config_002 (~8–12 GPU hours) due to ViT-L's larger parameter count and higher per-step compute, but this is justified as it is the most likely single change to yield the largest accuracy gain within our remaining 7-experiment budget.

Evidence: config_018 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) is the current best at 0.542 acc, clearly outperforming config_002 (resnet50) and confirming that multimodal + multiprofile + scgpt + imagenet_vit_l is the strongest backbone. The key untested dimension on this backbone is aggregation strategy. Question: Will transformer aggregation (config_015) outperform avgpool by capturing richer inter-profile relationships while retaining the proven scgpt/imagenet_vit_l/weighted-fusion components? Rationale: This is a minimal, high-information extension of the best config—only one variable (aggregation) changes, so any accuracy delta is cleanly attributable. Transformer aggregation is the most architecturally impactful remaining choice for multiprofile settings and could yield a meaningful jump over simple averaging. Expected cost: ~3.5–4.5 GPU hrs (moderately higher than config_018's 2.94 due to transformer attention over profiles, but well within budget with 6 experiments remaining and only 7.48 GPU hrs used so far).

Evidence: config_018 (scgpt, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the current best at 0.542 acc / 0.483 F1 with 2.94 GPU hrs. All top-performing configs use weighted fusion; concat fusion has not yet been tested in any multiprofile multimodal setting. Question: Does concat fusion outperform weighted fusion when paired with the best-known backbone (scgpt + ViT-L + avgpool)? This is a clean single-variable change from config_018, isolating the fusion strategy. Why this experiment: With 5 experiments remaining, confirming or rejecting concat fusion early is critical because it interacts with every other design choice (RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation). If concat is superior, subsequent experiments can pair it with alternative RNA encoders (scvi_n200, pca_n2000) for further gains. Expected cost is similar to config_018 (~2.9–3.0 GPU hrs) since the architecture is identical except for the fusion operation, making this a low-risk, high-information experiment.

The best result so far is config_018 (scgpt + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted, acc=0.542). Across the tested configs, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, avgpool > transformer, and weighted > concat, so the architecture is relatively well-optimized. The one major untested variable in this top-performing architecture is the RNA encoder: we've only tried scgpt. config_047 swaps scgpt for scvi_n200 while keeping the best image encoder, aggregation, and fusion. This directly tests whether a VAE-based RNA encoder captures complementary biological signal that could push accuracy above 0.542. Expected cost is similar to config_018 (~2.5–3.0 GPU hours) since the architecture is identical and scvi_n200 is a comparable or slightly smaller encoder than scgpt. With 4 experiments remaining, confirming or improving the RNA encoder choice in the best architecture is the highest-value next step before fine-tuning further.

The strongest result so far is config_047 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + avgpool + weighted) at 0.706 accuracy, dramatically outperforming all scgpt-based configs (~0.52–0.54). The only untested design axis holding all other parameters at their best-known values is aggregation: transformer vs. avgpool. With scgpt, avgpool beat transformer by ~2 pts (0.542 vs 0.520), but scvi_n200 produces a fundamentally different variational 200-dim representation where attention-based aggregation could capture inter-profile interactions that simple averaging misses. This single-variable change from the best config is the most interpretable and highest-value test: if transformer helps, we push accuracy above 0.706; if not, we confirm avgpool is optimal and can spend remaining budget on other axes (e.g., concat fusion or singleprofile). Expected cost: ~4–5 GPU hours (comparable to config_047's 4.82, with a modest increase from transformer attention layers), keeping total well within a reasonable budget for the remaining 3 experiments.

Evidence: config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the clear best at 0.7250 accuracy, and config_047 (same but avgpool) at 0.7062 confirms transformer aggregation helps. The only untested variant in this top-performing architecture family is config_016, which swaps weighted fusion for concat while keeping transformer aggregation. Question: Does concat fusion complement transformer aggregation differently than weighted fusion does—perhaps because the transformer already models cross-modal interactions that weighted fusion would redundantly re-weight? With 2 experiments remaining after this, confirming or ruling out concat in the best architecture is critical: if it matches or beats 0.7250, it opens a new direction; if not, we lock in config_026 as the likely optimum and can use remaining budget for a final confirmation or minor perturbation. Expected cost: ~3.5–4.0 GPU hours (same encoders and transformer aggregation as config_026, only fusion differs), making it comparable to the current best and well within budget.

The current best is config_026 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.725 accuracy. The evidence strongly identifies scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile as the dominant architecture, with transformer > avgpool (~0.02 gap) and weighted ≈ concat (~0.004 gap). Config_045 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, concat) is the only untested cell in this top-performing 2×2 aggregation×fusion grid. While it is unlikely to surpass 0.725, testing it completes the design-space characterization at relatively low cost (avgpool is cheaper than transformer; expected ~4–5 GPU hours, similar to config_047's 4.82). With only one experiment remaining, this is the best use of the budget: it either confirms config_026 as the definitive best or reveals a small interaction effect, while keeping total GPU hours manageable (~35 total). No other untested configuration (pca_n2000 variants, resnet50 variants, singleprofile variants) has a plausible path to beating 0.725 given the large encoder gaps observed.

The current best is config_026 (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) at 0.7250 accuracy. All four aggregation/fusion combinations with scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l have been tested, confirming transformer+weighted as optimal. The key remaining uncertainty is the image encoder's contribution when paired with the dominant scvi_n200 RNA encoder: in scgpt experiments, imagenet_vit_l beat resnet50 by ~1.7%, but with the much stronger scvi_n200 encoder the gap may narrow. Config_010 (scvi_n200 + resnet50 + transformer + weighted, multiprofile) tests this directly. If it approaches 0.725, it offers a significantly cheaper alternative (resnet50 is ~half the cost of imagenet_vit_l, estimated ~2.0–2.5 GPU hours vs ~3.6). If it underperforms, it confirms imagenet_vit_l is essential and locks in config_026 as the final answer. As the last experiment, this is the highest-information test among remaining options: it either finds a cheaper near-equivalent or definitively validates the current best. No other untested configuration (pca_n2000, singleprofile, rna_only) has a plausible path to exceeding 0.725 given the strong evidence for scvi_n200 + multimodal + multiprofile.
